# Getting started with Coral

Coral is an agentic IDE built for long-running autonomous agents and multi-agent teams. Give single agents or full engineering teams complex, multi-hour goals across your repositories while Coral coordinates their boards, tasks, and worktrees — and brings only the key decisions to you.

## Your Inbox and "Needs you"

Coral opens on the **Inbox** (the first tab in the top bar). The Inbox removes the need to jump from chat to chat — key decision points from all of your running agents and teams are sent directly to you. Questions from agents, permission prompts, and documents, images, or videos for review all show up in **Needs you**.

![The Inbox: Needs you lists every question, permission and file waiting on you](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Needs you**:

- **Getting started items:** On a new install, your first items walk you through getting an agent CLI ready, reading this guide, starting an agent, and making a team. Each item clears when you complete or dismiss it.
- **Questions and choices:** When an agent asks a question with buttons, click an answer right on the row or type a reply.
- **Permissions and terminal prompts:** When an agent needs permission to run a command or trust a folder, allow it from the row or click **Open agent**.
- **Files and plans for review:** When an agent uploads a plan, report, or screenshot tagged **For review**, click it to read, highlight lines to add comments, click **Send to agent** to discuss changes directly in the comment thread, and choose **Approve** or **Request changes**. Once you decide, the item leaves **Needs you**.

![A file waiting for review, with an inline comment thread and agent reply, Approve, and Request changes](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## Launching your first agent

Follow these steps to launch an agent:

1. **Click the Agents tab** in the top bar.
2. **Click New agent** at the bottom of the left sidebar (or press `Alt+N`), then pick a project folder on your computer.
3. **Make sure Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity is installed:** If none of them is installed yet, Coral opens the set-up dialog with the one-line install command, a **Copy** button, and **Check again**.
4. **Select No identity:** On the Persona step, leave it on **Blank: no persona** (no identity) or pick a preset, and click **Next**.
5. **Default to whatever model you want:** On the Agent step, pick your installed CLI (`Claude Code`, `Codex`, or `Antigravity`) and leave **Model** and **Thinking** on **Default** (or pick the specific model you prefer).
6. **Click Launch.**

![The New agent dialog: the agent CLI, its model and thinking level, and Launch](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

### Where your new agent shows up and how to use its controls

Once launched, your new agent appears in the **left sidebar** under the **Agents** tab. Click it to open its workspace. Across the top, you have the main navigation bar and the agent's own header bar:

![Zoomed-in view of the top navigation bar and the agent header bar](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

- **Top navigation bar** (across the very top of Coral): Switch between **Inbox**, **Agents**, **Automations**, **Skills**, **Analytics**, and **Docs**, or open **Settings** (the gear icon in the top-right corner).
- **Agent header bar** (across the top of the agent's pane):
  - **Search (`🔍`):** Search inside the conversation (`Ctrl+F` / `Cmd+F`).
  - **Pop out (`↗`):** Open this agent in its own standalone browser window.
  - **Pause notifications (`🔔` bell icon):** Pause incoming notifications and messages from team members and Coral while you are talking directly to the agent (the bell turns into a blue pause icon, and messages are held and delivered when you resume).

![Agent header controls showing Search, Pop out, Pause notifications (active bell on the left, paused on the right), and the Chat / Terminal toggle](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

  - **Right-hand panel toggle (`Files`, `Tasks`, `Notes`):** Show or hide the right-hand dock, which tracks every file the agent has changed (`+` / `-` diffs), its tasks, and saved notes.
  - **Switch between Chat view and Terminal view:** Use the **Chat / Terminal** toggle at the far right of the agent's header bar to switch between the clean **Chat view** and the live **Terminal view** (what the CLI itself is showing).

![Side-by-side comparison of the same agent in Chat view (left) and live Terminal view (right)](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Together, the left agent list, the center conversation or terminal pane, and the right-hand **Files**, **Tasks**, and **Notes** dock give you the agent's full workspace:

![An agent's full workspace: the agent list on the left, the conversation in the center, and changed files on the right](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## Starting a team and tracking Goals

A **team** is several agents working together on one shared message board, with an **Orchestrator** that coordinates the work.

1. **Open New team:** Click **New team** in your Inbox or at the bottom of the **Agents** sidebar.
2. **Pick a folder and roster:** Name the team, pick a project folder, and choose a template or add the roles you want (for example, an **Orchestrator**, a **Lead Dev**, and **QA**). Click **Launch**.
3. **Create a Goal or talk to the Orchestrator:** Click **New goal** in **Inbox > Goals** (or on the team page) to open the **New goal** screen, where you define the goal title, what should be true when it is done, and a checkable "done when" condition with live feedback from the **Guide** rail:

![The New goal screen: define the outcome, done-when check, and pictures with live Guide feedback](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

You can also tell the **Orchestrator** directly in chat what you want to build or fix — it breaks the work into **Goals** and **Tasks** on the board, assigns them to teammates, and sends only the key questions and review files to your **Inbox**.

You can track every team's high-level progress in **Inbox > Goals**, review your past decisions in **Inbox > Activity**, and browse every shared file in **Inbox > Artifacts**.

![Goals in the Inbox: each with its state, team and progress](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## What to try first

1. **Take the interactive single-agent tour:** In your Inbox, click **New agent** on the *Start your first agent* item. It pre-fills the **Getting started** tour prompt so the agent walks you through answering a button question in **Needs you** and reviewing a sample file.
2. **Try the 3-agent guided team tour:** In your Inbox, click **New team** on the *Make a team so agents can work together* item to launch a practice team (**Orchestrator**, **Lead Dev**, and **QA**) that demonstrates goals, tasks, and file reviews.
3. **Give an agent a real task on your code:** Click **New agent** (`Alt+N`), pick one of your own repositories, and ask it to explain the codebase, write an implementation plan and upload it **for review**, or fix a bug.

### Learn more on the Coral blog

To learn more about running long-running autonomous agents and multi-agent teams with Coral, read our engineering blog posts at **[coralhub.dev/blog](https://coralhub.dev/blog/)**:

- [Welcome to the Inbox](https://coralhub.dev/blog/welcome-to-the-inbox.html) — how the Inbox lets you manage autonomous agents without watching terminals.
- [Beta Testers Agent Team](https://coralhub.dev/blog/beta-testers-agent-team.html) — how a coordinated team of long-running agents tests and ships software continuously.
- [Using Coral's Context Reset to Reduce Average Turn Cost by 50–75%](https://coralhub.dev/blog/context-reset-turn-cost.html) — keeping long-running agents fast and cost-effective over multi-hour runs.
- [Search the Board Before Grepping Logs](https://coralhub.dev/blog/search-the-board-before-grepping-logs.html) — how long-running agent teams build and search shared institutional memory.
